Between two cities

Event Planners in Logan

Logan sits on the M1 between Brisbane and the Gold Coast, which means suppliers from both markets will travel here and a guest list split across the two can meet in the middle. Tell us the suburb, the date and the guest number, and planners covering the corridor can come back to you.

Halfway between two cities is a genuine planning advantage.

When half the guest list is in Brisbane and half is on the coast, an event in Logan asks everyone for the same 30 minutes rather than asking one side for an hour.

Logan sits directly between Brisbane and the Gold Coast, and the M1 runs through the middle of it. That single fact is the most useful thing to know about planning an event here. Suppliers from both cities quote this council area without argument, and a guest list drawn from both ends of the corridor can meet halfway instead of asking one half to drive an hour. People comparing event planners in Logan often start there rather than with a venue.

The second thing that shapes the local calendar is community. Logan is one of the most culturally diverse cities in Australia, with very large Pacific Islander, Maori, Indian and Vietnamese populations, and church halls and community centres carry far more of the celebration load here than they do elsewhere. West of the suburbs, Jimboomba, Munruben and Greenbank are acreage, so a marquee on a family property is ordinary rather than ambitious.

In and around Logan

What are you planning in Logan?

A lot of what happens here happens in a hall, on a property, or in a room chosen because both sides of the family can reach it. All three change how a planner works.

Start with

Weddings

Large guest lists and a hall or a hired room are the common shape, with catering brought in rather than supplied by the venue. That puts the kitchen, the bump in window and the bar arrangements on your side of the ledger, and it is where a planner earns the fee.

Find planners

Parties and milestones

Twenty firsts, fiftieths and church anniversaries here routinely run past 200 guests and are usually seated and catered. The venue question is often which hall, and the answer turns on the size of its kitchen and how many hours the booking actually covers.

Find planners

Corporate events

Logistics, transport and manufacturing employers along the motorway make up most of the local corporate calendar, so briefs lean towards depot open days, staff nights and long service presentations rather than black tie. Finish times are set by shift patterns, and the M1 decides what time people can realistically arrive.

Find planners

Engagement parties

An engagement here is frequently a full event rather than a drinks night, with a church component, a seated meal and a guest list of its own. Book the hall months ahead of the wedding. Rooms that seat 250 are committed a long way out, and the good Saturdays go first.

Find planners

Proposals

The Logan River and the reserves along it give you open water and shade close to the suburbs, and the acreage west of Park Ridge gives you a horizon. Both are best in the hour before sunset. Check what time gates on a reserve car park close, particularly in winter.

Find planners

Private celebrations

Church anniversaries, funerals, first communions and community fundraisers are a bigger share of the local calendar than they are in most council areas, and they tend to be catered for large numbers at short notice. Ask early what the hall allows you to cook on site and what has to arrive ready.

Planning support

How much help do you want in Logan?

The level you need usually follows the venue. A room that supplies catering, staff and a bar absorbs most of the risk. A hall you hire by the hour hands all of it back to you, and someone has to be holding it.

Full planning

A planner carries the whole build with you, from the first budget conversation to the last supplier leaving.

Usually engaged nine to fourteen months out.

  • Budget built and tracked
  • Venue and supplier shortlists
  • Contracts and payment schedule
  • Run sheet and floor plan
  • On the day, start to finish

Partial planning

You have made a start. A planner picks up the parts that have stalled and brings the rest into one plan.

Often engaged four to eight months out.

  • Picks up from where you are
  • Fills the supplier gaps
  • Tidies the budget
  • Builds the run sheet
  • Hands back a plan you can follow

On-the-day coordination

Your plan is built. A coordinator takes it over in the final weeks and runs the day so you can be in it.

Usually engaged four to eight weeks out.

  • Reads and stress-tests your plan
  • Confirms every supplier
  • Owns the run sheet
  • First point of contact on the day
  • Handles what goes sideways

Venue sourcing

Planners who know a market can shortlist against your date, your numbers and your budget rather than sending you back to the same search results.

Event coordination

Coordination is the execution layer: suppliers confirmed, a run sheet everyone has, and one person answering questions on the day.

Wedding coordination

A wedding coordinator takes a plan you have already built and runs the day itself, so nobody in the wedding party is directing traffic.

Choosing well

Finding the right planner in Logan

Three of these are about the room you have hired and one is about the motorway. In this council area those two things cause more trouble than budget ever does.

No. 01

Ask how they run a hall, not a venue

A hall gives you a room and a set of hours. Everything else, the catering, the bar, the tables, the linen, the staff and the cleaning, arrives with you and leaves with you. Ask a planner how many hall based events they have delivered, what the bump in window was, and who did the pack down at midnight. It is a different skill from managing a function centre.

No. 02

Read the hall booking hours before the guest list

Most hall hire agreements set an access time, a finish time and a clear out time, and the gap between them is smaller than people assume. Ask the planner to confirm all three in writing, plus what the kitchen is licensed to do and whether alcohol needs a separate permit. A four hour booking for a 200 guest seated dinner is not a four hour event.

No. 03

Ask whether they draw suppliers from both cities

Sitting between two markets is only an advantage if your planner uses it. Ask which of their caterers, hire companies and sound suppliers are based in Brisbane and which on the Gold Coast, and whether either charges to come to Logan. On a tight budget the second quote from the other direction is often the one that lands.

No. 04

Make them check the M1 at the right hour

A Friday afternoon on the motorway is a different road from a Tuesday morning, and a guest list arriving from both directions hits it at the same time. Ask whether the travel legs in the run sheet were checked on the day and hour you will actually run, and what the plan is if the southbound traffic stops. Coaches sit in it too.

A hall gives you four walls and a clock. Everything else you bring, and someone has to run it.

On the ground

The motorway, the hall and the acreage

Three local realities explain most of what makes a Logan run sheet different: where the guests come from, what kind of room they are coming to, and how far west the address sits.

Being in the middle is worth money

Logan is the meeting point of two supplier markets. Brisbane companies come south and Gold Coast companies come north, and neither treats this council area as a long trip, which means you can genuinely compare quotes from two cities on the same job. Use it. The same logic applies to guests: a family split between the northern suburbs and the coast can be asked for half an hour each rather than an hour from one side. That changes what time the ceremony can start and how many people stay to the end.

Halls and churches carry the calendar

Community halls, church halls and cultural association buildings host a large share of celebrations here, which is unusual in a metropolitan council area and it changes the work completely. A hall is a booking, not a service. You bring the catering, the bar, the tables, the linen, the sound and the cleaning, and you return the room empty by a stated hour. The good ones are booked out for Saturdays a long way ahead, particularly the halls with a full kitchen, so the room often has to be confirmed before the date is announced.

The western half is country

Jimboomba, Munruben, Greenbank and Park Ridge are acreage rather than suburb, so a marquee on a family block is a normal local brief. It is also a build, and the checklist is the same one every property event carries.

  • Generator capacity for lighting, catering and sound
  • Bathrooms once the guest number passes about 80
  • Parking on grass, with a marshal and a lit walking route
  • A wet weather structure agreed before the deposit
  • Drive times to the western suburbs checked, not estimated

Questions

Planning an event in Logan

How much does an event planner cost in Logan?

Airtasker, updated February 2025, puts event planning in Australia at $1,000 to $20,000 with a median near $8,000, hourly rates of $70 to $120, and 10 to 15 per cent of total budget as a common alternative. In this council area the venue type moves the number as much as the guest count, because a hall event asks a planner to source and manage everything a function centre would otherwise supply.

We have booked a community hall. What does a planner actually do?

Everything the hall does not, which is most of it. A hall hands you a room between two stated hours, so the planner sources the catering, the tables, the linen, the bar, the sound and the cleaning, sets a bump in schedule that fits inside your access time, and makes sure the room is empty by the clear out hour. Ask for that schedule in writing. On a 200 guest seated dinner the pack down is the part that runs late.

Do Gold Coast and Brisbane suppliers both work in Logan?

Both do, and that is the practical advantage of sitting on the M1 halfway between them. A caterer in the southern Brisbane suburbs and one on the northern Gold Coast are each about 30 minutes away, so you can compare two markets on the same brief. Ask whether either adds a travel charge for Logan addresses, and ask again for the western suburbs, since Jimboomba and Greenbank are a further run for both.

How much time should we allow for guests travelling on the M1?

Check the route at the day and hour you will actually drive it, then add a buffer, because a Friday afternoon on the motorway behaves nothing like a weekday morning. Guests arriving from Brisbane and from the coast hit the same peak from opposite directions, so a 5pm ceremony pulls both halves of the room into the worst of it. A late morning or a Sunday start avoids the problem entirely if your date allows.

Can we hold a marquee reception at Jimboomba or Greenbank?

Yes, and it is ordinary out there rather than unusual, because those suburbs are acreage. Treat it as a build. You are supplying power, water, bathrooms above about 80 guests, lighting, a wet weather structure and parking on grass with a lit route back to the cars. Confirm the driveway takes a loaded truck and that a coach can turn. Then confirm the ground, since a wet week in the summer months changes what a paddock will carry.

How far ahead should we book for a large Logan event?

Start with the room, not the planner, if your guest list is above about 200. The halls and function rooms that take those numbers are committed for Saturdays a long way out, and the cool dry months from April to September go first. Nine to fourteen months is a reasonable window for full planning, four to eight months for partial, and four to eight weeks for coordination alone. If the date is already fixed, chase the room this week.
